body:

What I find this app is missing and why I didn’t give it five stars is how it doesn’t provide you with an option to remind yourself 15min before the event. If there was an option to select drive or travel time - I feel it would help so many to plan for how long it takes to get to your appointment. Right now I have to include the time the appointment is in the title and set the timer for approx 30 min down to 15 minutes depending on the distance and weather. 

I would also like to be able to select some reminders to not be able to push to my smart watch. If say medication reminders can be pushed but the minor less urgent reminds don’t and just appear on my phone. That would be lovely.

Thanks!

title: The Best
body:
I don’t normally write reviews for app but this one is an exception. Due is exactly what I needed. A fast and easy to use reminder app. I don’t need anything complicated like different folders or sections. I just need a list of reminders and I need the app to work perfectly on my phone,ipad and most importantly my Apple Watch that will remind me when it matters.

Due check all those boxes. My favorite feature is that the smart language is extremely powerfull while supporting multiple languages (I can write ‘tomorrow’ or ‘demain’ which is french for tomorrow and both will work) and it takes me only a mere second to create a new reminder. 

I can also snooze or report a reminder easily with the little menu either from notification or on my phone or Apple Watch.

If you run your life with reminders like me then Due is a most have. Give it a try and stick with it for a couple of days and you’ll never go back to your old app or workflow.

title: My most used reminder app
body:
Due is there for those things that you have to deal with immediately. I won’t claim that it’s the only reminder app that you need, but I find it to be my most used one. 
I use the app in two ways: 
1) either for things (either important or frivolous) that I need to do on another app or remember later, but I don’t want to do immediately because I’m with family, in a meeting etc. 
2) things that I just cannot put off.
The relentless reminders are invaluable to me, and anyone who can’t afford to miss a reminder. I don’t always check my to-do lists on other apps, but due makes it impossible for me to procrastinate the tasks that I set on it. Even if I miss the first notification, it will eventually get my attention  
There is no other reminder app that has less frills, and Due allows me to input reminders faster than any other app that I’ve tried. The quick time selections allow me to be reminded at times that I’m likely to have the time to deal with it.
I’m looking forward to trying version 3, and will always pay for the new version of this app, especially considering the low price point and the amount of use that I get from it. 
Kudos to the developer for keeping it around for as long as it has been, and for resisting the urge to turn it into a bulky program.

title: Great new update, but a couple of bugs
body:
This app was already the best reminder app I have ever found, but now it has been even further improved. I will never look for another reminders app again. 

However, do not use the "sync to Dropbox" feature. It causes the app to freeze and crash a lot when it is enabled. After realizing this I tried turning off all syncing options, but this didn't stop it from syncing. I actually had to unlink it from my Dropbox account to restore the non-crashy performance.

Another thing, be careful when swiping left to mark a reminder as completed. If you swipe too far, you will delete it instead. That is easy to do. This will only be a problem if you are marking a REPEATING item however, as it will prevent all future occurrences of the reminder when you delete it. Otherwise I imagine most people probably wouldn't care if they delete an item or just mark it as done. If you do delete it, there is a handy red "undo delete" bar that appears at the bottom of the screen briefly. And if you realize your error after this bar has vanished, "shake to undo" will still undo the delete if you have not done anything since. Of course when you swipe left on an item, it happens so fast you might not realize you have deleted something instead of only marking it as done. This is something to pay close attention to.

Other than these issues, it is a wonderful app and I love the new update. It is much more customizable than before. And the 45 new notification sounds that have been added are really cool sounds!! Well done (and please fix the bugs)!

title: Great App for Enhancing Task Managers
body:

This keeps my Things task manager and calendar cleaner and encourages me to manage talks I might not log due to time it takes in other apps.

If you get annoyed figuring out if you want something in Due, Reminders, Notes, Things, Calendar, all of them, etc. I highly recommend Drafts, my new favorite iOS app. It allows quick note capture and two tap publish to a large list of apps, including Due. It also allows tweeting. Is it a task, event, idea, tweet, or beginning of a blog post? Decide after you write it. Drafts will also allow multiple sends if you want your text in multiple apps.

My two requests for Due- I wish the 1min default snooze could be 5- it's not useful at 1min and 1hr only. 1min distracts, and I have to turn of the alarm (or reschedule, but then there is no snooze). Also a "send to calendar" or other apps (Reminders, Things) would be nice.

title: Adequate, But Looking for Something Better
body:
Due gets the job done in spite of itself. It has two downfalls.

First, the out-of-the-box settings result in it nagging you incessantly, and the default due time is two minutes in the future. So you have to go diving into settings, but only after you realise the thing is driving you nuts with its nagging. 

Second, the user interface has that common affliction nowadays - it tries to look minimalist and slick. This comes about from having too many propeller-heads designing things without input from real users. Consequently there's far to many darned buttons to push to do a simple thing like set up a reminder or reschedule it.

title: Finally
body: For those who just transfered from blackberry, this is the closest it gets to blackberry calendar(reminders) finally you can snooze with an iphone. Theres even a customizable alert, suppose you have something to do on wednesdays and sayurdays for the next 4 months or so, you dont have to enter it manually for each time. Only bad thing about this app is that if a reminder is not on autosnooze and the phone autolocks, it disappears ( but at least you still have the badge number showing) so you can compare that to the blackberry's flashing LED . Other thing is the 1 minute or 1 hour only autosnooze ... No choice here, this is what apple designers give you so youll find nothing better for reminders than this app on iphone
